A1.justification: Both PDFs describe BALROG and contain readable main text, figures, tables, and Appendices A–F. Content can be matched across additions and renumbering; internal reporting inconsistencies do not prevent comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original model evaluations across six game environments, trajectory analyses, and a NetHack knowledge questionnaire.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark evaluations and adds Claude 3.5 Haiku results and a Crafter rendering experiment in Appendix B.3.

M1.justification: The agent–environment framework, zero-shot action-generation procedure, observation handling, and NetHack progression metric remain unchanged. The new Crafter rendering condition tests existing agents rather than introducing a new agent algorithm.

E1.justification: Appendix B.3 adds Crafter observations rendered with Minecraft-style 3D models and textures, extending visual input conditions. Appendix E changes the reported MiniHack Quest coverage from Easy, Medium, and Hard to Easy and Medium. The six principal game environments remain.

E2.justification: Claude 3.5 Haiku is added to language-only comparisons across all six games, while o1-mini is removed from the NetHack comparison. Additional Llama rows in the TextWorld and MiniHack tables were already represented in v1 Figure 2, so these are not new comparators.

E3.justification: The new Crafter experiment compares performance under 2D and 3D rendering. MiniHack's stated Quest difficulty selection also changes. The zero-shot protocol, 16-observation history, and scoring rules remain unchanged; the PDFs do not establish whether the revised MiniHack description reflects rerunning experiments.

E4.justification: Appendix B.3 and Table 8 add a focused seven-model analysis testing whether more familiar Minecraft-style rendering alleviates VLM failures. Existing trajectory analyses and the Appendix F.5 knowing-doing questionnaire are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same stated seed counts and standard-error reporting, including 25 seeds per BabyAI task and 10 for Crafter. The new rendering table uses the existing mean-plus-error format; no increased run counts or new statistical procedures are reported.

E6.justification: Substantial numerical revisions alter reported rankings: Table 2 changes Sonnet from 29.98% to 32.64%, above GPT-4o's unchanged 32.34%; Sonnet's BabyAI VLM score changes from 50% to 82% in Table 5. Haiku and 3D Crafter results are added, with further Crafter and NetHack value revisions. These are reported score changes, not established same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: Appendix F.2 retains the same progression definition based on human winning probabilities at attained dungeon and experience levels, taking the higher progression value. No new mathematical assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs appear.

C1.justification: The abstract qualifies the vision-degradation claim by changing 'models perform worse' to 'several models perform worse.' The benchmark, progression metric, long-horizon difficulty, and knowing-doing-gap contributions remain substantively unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix B.3 interprets the rendering experiment as suggesting limitations beyond texture familiarity, while calling the findings preliminary. Section 4 removes v1's speculation that adding vision capabilities to Llama 3.2 harmed its linguistic and reasoning abilities.

D1.justification: Section 3.3 newly specifies the October 22, 2024 Claude releases, and Appendix B.3 identifies Minecraft models and textures used for rendering. The release disclosure does not establish that Sonnet's checkpoint changed. Existing prompts, wrappers, and code-access information are retained.

R1.justification: Section 5 and the bibliography add Ruoss et al.'s LMACT benchmark. The broader positioning relative to agent benchmarks, game environments, and long-context reasoning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Most prose and section organization are retained. Local revisions update the abstract and results discussion, add Appendix B.3 and acknowledgments, and revise affiliations, publication headers, and contribution wording.

P2.justification: v2 adds the 3D Crafter illustration and rendering-comparison table, updates Figure 2, and replaces the MiniHack Quest Hard illustration with an Easy example. Figures 1–2 replace 'AgentQuest' with 'BALROG'; tables gain or reorder rows, and subsequent displays are renumbered.

improvement.justification: The new Crafter control provides evidence about a previously untested explanation for VLM failures, while the qualified abstract and removal of speculative reasoning improve claim calibration. These are limited gains: v2 Tables 7 and 8 give conflicting Llama Crafter baselines, and the retained claim that Sonnet is o1-preview's closest NetHack competitor overlooks the newly added Haiku result. These inconsistencies weaken the updated interpretation.
